catalog.title: Open a canonical DocForge project
catalog.goal: Prove directory and manifest project entry use the strict DocForge v1 contract.
preconditions: The repository test fixtures and Python environment are available.

steps.action: Run project model, loader, and application project service tests.
steps.expected: Canonical directories and docforge.yaml open while bare Markdown and obsolete manifests are rejected.

assertions.statement: The strict DocForge project entry contract passes.

catalog.title: Verify repository and release delivery contracts
catalog.goal: Prove active repository surfaces and local release artifacts use DocForge identities and neutral filenames.
preconditions: Repository facticity, distribution, and local release artifacts are available.

steps.action: Run facticity, desktop distribution, and release metadata validation.
steps.expected: Active findings remain zero and local release artifacts satisfy DocForge naming and integrity rules.

assertions.statement: Repository-owned and local release surfaces use the DocForge delivery contract.

args: set -eu; PYTHONPATH=src .venv/bin/python scripts/check_facticity.py --json /tmp/docforge-case-a10.json --markdown /tmp/docforge-case-a10.md; PYTHONPATH=src .venv/bin/python scripts/verify_desktop_distribution.py --platform macos --bundle-root src-tauri/target/release/bundle; PYTHONPATH=src .venv/bin/python scripts/prepare_release.py --tag v0.1.0 --validate-only

catalog.title: Build a general DocForge project
catalog.goal: Prove a neutral general project completes inspect, validate, review, and build without academic metadata.
preconditions: The docforge-general fixture and Python environment are available.

steps.action: Copy the general fixture to an isolated directory and run all four CLI operations.
steps.expected: All operations succeed and create neutral Review and DOCX outputs.

assertions.statement: The general project completes the neutral offline flow without academic requirements.

args: set -eu; tmp=$(mktemp -d /tmp/docforge-a2.XXXXXX); trap 'rm -rf "$tmp"' EXIT; cp -R tests/fixtures/docforge-general "$tmp/project"; PYTHONPATH=src .venv/bin/python -m docforge.cli inspect "$tmp/project" >/dev/null; PYTHONPATH=src .venv/bin/python -m docforge.cli validate "$tmp/project" >/dev/null; PYTHONPATH=src .venv/bin/python -m docforge.cli review "$tmp/project" >/dev/null; PYTHONPATH=src .venv/bin/python -m docforge.cli build "$tmp/project" >/dev/null; test -s "$tmp/project/review/document.review.md"; test -s "$tmp/project/review/document.review-map.json"; test -s "$tmp/project/build/document.docx"

catalog.title: Build an academic profile without global leakage
catalog.goal: Prove academic fields are typed and template-scoped while general documents remain valid.
preconditions: The academic and general fixtures are available.

steps.action: Run template, compiler, project, and distribution profile tests.
steps.expected: Academic builds pass and general builds remain free of academic requirements.

assertions.statement: Academic profile requirements do not leak into general projects.

args: PYTHONPATH=src .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/templates tests/compiler tests/project tests/test_distribution.py -q

catalog.title: Reject obsolete ThesisForge contracts
catalog.goal: Prove obsolete active identities are absent or rejected without aliases.
preconditions: Repository facticity rules and obsolete-input tests are available.

steps.action: Run obsolete-domain tests and the repository facticity scan.
steps.expected: All negative contracts are rejected and active finding count is zero.

assertions.statement: No obsolete ThesisForge contract remains active.

args: set -eu; PYTHONPATH=src .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/test_facticity.py tests/core/test_forge_document.py tests/project -q; PYTHONPATH=src .venv/bin/python scripts/check_facticity.py --json /tmp/docforge-case-a4.json --markdown /tmp/docforge-case-a4.md

catalog.title: Use neutral source, build, and Review defaults
catalog.goal: Prove canonical filenames match across project, CLI, runtime, and desktop contracts.
preconditions: CLI, project, protocol, and distribution tests are available.

steps.action: Run project, CLI, contract, and desktop distribution default-path tests.
steps.expected: All layers use document.md and neutral document output paths.

assertions.statement: Canonical neutral default paths match across all product layers.

args: PYTHONPATH=src .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/project tests/cli tests/contracts tests/test_desktop_distribution.py -q

catalog.title: Enforce project path security
catalog.goal: Prove safe project-relative resources are accepted and unsafe path classes are rejected.
preconditions: Project loader and application path-security tests are available.

steps.action: Run project path and application service redteam tests.
steps.expected: Absolute, remote, traversal, and symlink-escape paths fail with stable diagnostics.

assertions.statement: All unsafe project path classes are rejected without weakening safe relative paths.

args: set -eu; PYTHONPATH=src .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/project tests/application/test_project_services.py -q; /Users/wenliang_zeng/.cargo/bin/cargo test --manifest-path src-tauri/Cargo.toml project_tests

catalog.title: Preserve the deterministic DOCX pipeline
catalog.goal: Prove semantic ordering, renderer boundaries, OOXML structures, cancellation, deterministic output, and atomic replacement.
preconditions: Core, compiler, renderer, application, and deterministic-output tests are available.

steps.action: Run core, compiler, DOCX renderer, acceptance, and build lifecycle tests.
steps.expected: The ordered deterministic pipeline and real OOXML structures pass.

assertions.statement: The semantic-to-DOCX pipeline remains deterministic, ordered, cancelable, and atomic.

args: PYTHONPATH=src .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/core tests/compiler tests/renderers/docx tests/application tests/test_acceptance.py tests/test_compiler.py tests/test_docx_renderer.py -q

catalog.title: Keep Python, TypeScript, Rust, HTTP, and Tauri protocol parity
catalog.goal: Prove all runtime boundaries use one strict versioned DocForge protocol and BuildReport identity.
preconditions: Python, frontend, and Rust dependencies are installed in the verification worktree.

steps.action: Run focused Python adapters, frontend transport tests, real HTTP acceptance, and Rust protocol tests.
steps.expected: All runtimes accept canonical identities and reject obsolete or malformed protocol data.

assertions.statement: The versioned DocForge runtime and BuildReport contract is consistent across all boundaries.

args: set -eu; PYTHONPATH=src .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/adapters tests/application/test_build_report_contract.py tests/application/test_build_stage_lifecycle.py -q; /Users/wenliang_zeng/.nvm/versions/node/v22.19.0/bin/pnpm --dir frontend test; /Users/wenliang_zeng/.cargo/bin/cargo test --manifest-path src-tauri/Cargo.toml

catalog.title: Verify installed DocForge and Microsoft Word preview evidence
catalog.goal: Prove the installed macOS workbench uses neutral terminology and generated a valid Word PDF preview.
preconditions: The content-addressed installed acceptance receipt and screenshot are present.

steps.action: Validate the installed app receipt, Microsoft Word result, accessibility labels, and screenshot SHA-256.
steps.expected: The receipt is passed, Word preview is available, and the screenshot matches its recorded hash.

assertions.statement: Installed DocForge.app and Microsoft Word final preview evidence is internally consistent and content-addressed.

args: PYTHONPATH=src .venv/bin/python -c 'import hashlib,json,pathlib; root=pathlib.Path("openspec/changes/docforge-project-format-v1/development/tasks/006-workbench-desktop/evidence"); r=json.loads((root/"macos-native-acceptance.json").read_text()); p=root/r["evidence"]["screenshot"]; assert r["ok"] is True and r["status"]=="passed"; assert r["app"]["displayName"]=="DocForge" and r["runtime"]["manifest"]=="docforge.yaml" and r["runtime"]["source"]=="document.md"; assert r["build"]["output"]=="document.docx" and r["wordPreview"]["engine"]=="microsoft-word" and r["wordPreview"]["status"]=="available" and r["wordPreview"]["pdfGenerated"] is True; assert hashlib.sha256(p.read_bytes()).hexdigest()==r["evidence"]["screenshotSha256"]; assert r["bundleVerification"]["ok"] is True; print(json.dumps({"ok":True,"word":r["wordPreview"]["microsoftWordVersion"],"screenshotSha256":r["evidence"]["screenshotSha256"]}))'

failures.summary: The approved command runner omitted the assertion protocol required to produce structured assertion_result evidence.
failures.root_cause: The case contract declared env_keys=[], so the Runtime did not inject SPECNAV_VERIFICATION_ASSERTION_IDS or SPECNAV_VERIFICATION_ASSERTION_RESULT_FILE and no authoritative oracle result was emitted.

args: set -eu; PYTHONPATH=src .venv/bin/python scripts/check_facticity.py --json /tmp/docforge-case-a10.json --markdown /tmp/docforge-case-a10.md; PYTHONPATH=src .venv/bin/python scripts/verify_desktop_distribution.py --platform macos --bundle-root src-tauri/target/release/bundle; PYTHONPATH=src .venv/bin/python scripts/prepare_release.py --tag v0.1.0 --validate-only

failures.summary: The approved command runner omitted the assertion protocol and did not expose the required toolchain PATH.
failures.root_cause: The case contract declared env_keys=[] and relied on ambient PATH, so the Runtime could neither inject SPECNAV assertion output variables nor consistently locate Rust/Node toolchains.
